lines.name: vs. ...d5 and ...e6
lines.intro: The London is a system: you play the same setup in almost every game. Get the bishop out to f4 before e3, then build a triangle of pawns on c3, d4 and e3.

notes.1: Black meets you in the center.
notes.2: The London bishop comes out before e3 can lock it in.
notes.4: Support d4 and open the f1 bishop.
notes.8: Hold d4 with c3. That completes the London pawn triangle.
notes.9: Black adds more pressure on d4.
notes.10: Develop the knight behind your pawns, ready to support e4 or Ne5.
notes.11: Black offers to trade off your good bishop.
notes.12: Step back to g3 instead of trading. If Black takes, hxg3 gives you a half-open h-file.
notes.14: Put the bishop on d3, aiming at h7.

lines.name: vs. King's Indian setup
lines.intro: Against ...g6 and ...Bg7, keep the same setup, but play h3 so your bishop has a safe square on h2.

notes.1: Black develops and keeps options open.
notes.2: The London bishop comes out before e3 can lock it in.
notes.3: Black plans to fianchetto the bishop.
notes.4: Support d4 and open the f1 bishop.
notes.5: The bishop on g7 aims at your center.
notes.8: A quiet square. Against this setup the bishop doesn't need to be on d3.
notes.10: h3 gives your bishop a retreat on h2 if ...Nh5 comes, and stops ...Bg4.

lines.name: vs. early ...c5 and ...Qb6
lines.intro: When Black hits d4 early and brings the queen to b6 to attack b2, the simplest answer is to offer a queen trade with Qb3.

notes.1: Black meets you in the center.
notes.2: The London bishop comes out before e3 can lock it in.
notes.9: The queen attacks b2, which your bishop no longer defends now that it has left c1.
notes.10: Offer a queen trade. If Black takes, axb3 opens the a-file for your rook.
